## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
# Vegan is a R package designed for community ecologists
# Vegan's has most basic functions of community ordination,
# diversity analysis, and dissimilarity analysis.
#
# Link to vignette:
# https://vegandevs.r-universe.dev/vegan/doc/intro-vegan.pdf



# ------Install & Run Vegan and other packages------
install.packages("vegan", repos = "https://vegandevs.github.io/vegan/")
install.packages("ape", repos = "https://github.com/emmanuelparadis/ape")

library(ape)
library(vegan)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)

# ------Data sets------
data(package = "vegan")

# we will be working with Vegetation and Environment in Dutch
# Dune Meadows.

data("dune")
str(dune)




# --------ordination--------
# Ordination, also referred to as gradient analysis, is a
# multivariate analysis that is typically used to explore data.
# In ordination space, points that are similar to each other
# share similar traits. Ordination is used to analyze sets of
# multivariate objects, which are common in community ecology,
# systems biology, and genetics.

### Detrended correspondence analysis (DCA) ###
# DCA is used to find the main factors in data sets that
# are species rich but that may have sparse data matrices

ord_dca <- decorana(dune)
decorana (veg = dune)
# decorana is the command for detrended correspondence analysis
scores(ord_dca)
# shows the actual ordination results

plot(ord_dca, type = "n") |>
  points("sites", cex = 0.8, pch=21, col="red", bg="yellow") |>
  text("species", cex=0.7, col="blue")
# plots the results from the DCA

### Non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) ###
# Non-metric multidimensional scaling uses a distance to show the
# similarity or dissimilarity in the groups.


ord <- metaMDS(dune, trace = FALSE)
# metaMDS is the command for non-metric multi dimensional analysis
ord # get results

plot(ord, type = "n") |>
  points("sites", cex = 0.8, pch=21, col="red", bg="yellow") |>
  text("species", cex=0.7, col="blue")
# plots the results from the NMDS

# ----------graphics------------

# we have graphed the results of two ordination methods (DCA and NMDS)
# Points can be selected for an labeled differently with various functions
# the vegan package

data(dune.env) #load a different built in data set
attach(dune.env)
plot(ord, disp="sites", type="n") # base plot
ordihull(ord, Management, col=1:4, lwd=3) # draws color coordinated convex hulls
ordiellipse(ord, Management, col=1:4, kind = "ehull", lwd=3) # draws color coordinated ellipsoid hulls with standard deviation
ordiellipse(ord, Management, col=1:4, draw="polygon") #fills in actual data
ordispider(ord, Management, col=1:4, label = TRUE) #combines the cross sections of the ellipses principal axes
points(ord, disp="sites", pch=21, col="red", bg="yellow", cex=1.3) #marks the ends of the cross sections

# ----------Fitting environmental variables-------------
# vegan has two functions for fitting env. variables
# envfit for vectors of continuous variables and centroids of levels of class variables
# ordisurf for smooth surfaces of continuous variables and isotropic spline surfaces

ord.fit <- envfit(ord ~ A1 + Management, data=dune.env, perm=999)
ord.fit

# Envfit can asses the significance of the variables with a permutation test

plot(ord, dis="site")
plot(ord.fit, bg = "yellow")

# plot results

ordisurf(ord, A1, add=TRUE)
# adds fitted surface onto the ordination, returns the results of the fitted gam

# -------------Constrained Ordination-------------
# constrained ordination as defined by Ramette 2007 "In constrained
# (canonical) ordination analyses, only the variation in the species
# table that can be explained by the environmental variables is displayed
# and analyzed, and not all the variation in the species table.”
# it is not reccomended by the authors of the package to add in all
# environmental variables, the result could be similar to unconstrained ordination

# I do not fully understand the difference between constrained and unconstrained
# ordination methods.

ord <- cca(dune ~ A1 + Management, data=dune.env) #canonical correspondence analysis
ord

plot(ord, spe.par = list(optimize = TRUE), sit.par = list(type="p"))
# plotted results of the canonical correspondence analyses

# Vegan includes a test for the significance of the constraints that mimics
# a standard anova test

anova(ord)
# R automatically chooses the correct anova variant

# Vegan allows us to partial out the effects of constraints
ord <- cca(dune ~ A1 + Management + Condition(Moisture), data=dune.env)
ord

# This can influence the significance, in the following anova the effect of
# moisture is removed
anova(ord, by="term")

# this concludes the introduction vignette into Vegan, I will now look at a few of the other
# common functions

# ------------Ecological Diversity-------------
data(BCI)

# Diversity Indicies

#shannon diversity index
H <- diversity(BCI)
H
# Finds the diversity indicies for all sites in the data set

#Pielou's evenness
J <- H/log(specnumber(BCI))
J
# specnumber is funciton in vegan to find the number of species

# Fisher log-series as a diversity index
alpha <- fisher.alpha(BCI)
alpha


# -----------Vegan Package------------------
### Example 1: Unconstrained ordination
## NMDS
data(varespec)
data(varechem)
ord <- metaMDS(varespec)
plot(ord, type = "t")
## Fit environmental variables
ef <- envfit(ord, varechem)
ef
plot(ef, p.max = 0.05)
### Example 2: Constrained ordination (RDA)
## The example uses formula interface to define the model
data(dune)
data(dune.env)
## No constraints: PCA
mod0 <- rda(dune ~ 1, dune.env)
mod0
plot(mod0)


## All environmental variables: Full model
mod1 <- rda(dune ~ ., dune.env)
mod1
plot(mod1)
## Automatic selection of variables by permutation P-values
mod <- ordistep(mod0, scope=formula(mod1))
mod
plot(mod)
## Permutation test for all variables
anova(mod)
## Permutation test of "type III" effects, or significance when a term
## is added to the model after all other terms
anova(mod, by = "margin")
## Plot only sample plots, use different symbols and draw SD ellipses
## for Managemenet classes
plot(mod, display = "sites", type = "n")
with(dune.env, points(mod, disp = "si", pch = as.numeric(Management)))
with(dune.env, legend("topleft", levels(Management), pch = 1:4,
                      title = "Management"))
with(dune.env, ordiellipse(mod, Management, label = TRUE))
## add fitted surface of diversity to the model
ordisurf(mod, diversity(dune), add = TRUE)
### Example 3: analysis of dissimilarites a.k.a. non-parametric
### permutational anova
adonis2(dune ~ ., dune.env)
adonis2(dune ~ Management + Moisture, dune.env)


# More for PCA
# help from https://rpubs.com/brouwern/veganpca
data("iris")
my.rda <- rda(iris[,-5])
biplot(my.rda,
       display = c("sites",
                   "species"),
       type = c("text",
                "points"))
#Add hulls
ordihull(my.rda,
         group = iris$Species,
         col = c(1,2,3))


#Add legend
spp.names <- levels(iris$Species)
legend("topright",
       col = c(1,2,3),
       lty = 1,
       legend = spp.names)

1 + 1
```

2 * 2
